content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I currently have a setup that accurately calculates machine uptime as a live percentage on the operator panel, with a reset button used every 8 hours. The issue is that when the machine must be turned off due to a fault, all the runtime data is erased. Is there a way to store this information so it can be resumed when the machine is powered back on?
Which device do you mean is powered down—the operator panel or the [product_name] module?
It's the [product_name] module; when the machine is shut off, power to the [product_name] is also removed as it receives its 24V supply from the machine.

I can't check this right now as I don't have access to an operator panel. However, if certain function blocks in the [product_name] program don't have data retention enabled, such as with stopwatch blocks, their values will be lost when power is removed.
Is there a way to make sure these values are kept?
Enable the data retention setting for those blocks.

analysis.insight_summary: Community members note that when the [product_name] module loses power, runtime data like accumulated uptime is cleared, leading to inconvenience and loss of essential operational data. The main usability issue discussed is the absence of automatic data retention across power cycles, which affects features such as uptime calculations that depend on memory persistence. The conversation indicates some confusion about device behavior and a need for clearer methods to achieve data retention.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [product_name] module to retain operational counters and similar data even during power-off events, allowing them to continue processes without impact from data loss.
